canonical_names: The canonical spelling is the name printed and the name a page is titled with, so it is the player's real name rather than whichever spelling the data happens to use most. Suffixes are written the way the rest of the data writes them, with no full stop. The alias keys are the raw spellings in data.json and never change: they are what matches. Marcus Thornton II was in here until the build began joining on a person: bio.csv has one Marcus Thornton, the 2009 LSU guard, and no row for the man paid in 2017-18, so the two are not one career and the II is not a fuller spelling of the I. He is not the LSU man's son either: data/bio_overrides.json names him as the William & Mary guard born in 1993, taken 45th in 2015, no relation.

readme: Two spellings of one player, merged into one identity for the engine. Read by scripts/factoids.py and reusable by the prerender script; build_data.py and data.json are untouched. Without this, each half looks like a separate short career: the older spelling looks finished and the newer one starts mid-career with the other half's running total already on it. Candidate rule and evidence below; the canonical spelling is the one the data uses most, and on a tie the one carrying the most recent season.
rule: Names that match once Jr / Sr / II / III / IV / V, full stops and apostrophes are stripped, with the same draft year (or one missing), no season in common, and seasons that run continuously together (no gap longer than 1 season). A shared season means two men; a hole in the run is a career gap, which data/identity_splits.json handles instead.

one_mans_name_misspelled_in_a_sheet.note: A sheet spelling one man's name wrong, mapped to his own spelling. Read by build_data.py, so the two rows land on one person in data.json rather than on two: these are not two spellings of one career, which alias_to_canonical above handles after the build, but a typo in a single season's row. The misspelled half shows up as a man who was paid and never played, with a player page of his own, and his money is the real man's money counted a second time.
one_mans_name_misspelled_in_a_sheet.rule: The same man, the same season and the same club, with the same figure or within a dollar of it, where one spelling has the games and the other has none, or neither does. Deliberately not the rule above: these spellings share a season, which for two careers would mean two men, and the difference is a letter rather than a suffix. Each pair is checked by hand and the evidence is written down below. The canonical spelling is the man's real name, which is the one the stats sheet and bio.csv carry where they carry him at all.
